violations.title: FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY missing
violations.message: Table public.profiles_public has RLS enabled but not FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. The table owner role still bypasses RLS, which often masks broken policies in development and CI. Run `ALTER TABLE public.profiles_public FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;`.

violations.title: Policy expression does not reference any column of the table
violations.message: Policy 'anyone can read profiles' on public.profiles_public does not reference any column of the table. The predicate is purely session-state — every row is admitted or denied based on configuration alone. Add a row-level condition (e.g. tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant')).

violations.title: All policies on table are permissive
violations.message: Every policy on public.profiles_public is permissive. Permissive policies combine with OR — adding one RESTRICTIVE policy gives a floor (e.g. tenant scoping) that no OR branch can bypass, for the roles in its own TO list. Use TO PUBLIC to bind every role: measured, a restrictive TO authenticated left authenticated at 1 row and another role at 3.

violations.title: Permissive policy USING clause is constant true
violations.message: Policy 'anyone can read profiles' on public.profiles_public has USING (true), which admits every row to every caller in the role list. Replace with a real predicate or remove the policy.

violations.title: RLS-enabled table has no write-side policy
violations.message: Table public.profiles_public has RLS enabled and 1 policy, but every policy is FOR SELECT — no policy covers INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE. With RLS enforced and no write-side policy, writes by non-owner roles are denied: INSERT raises a row-violates-policy error, while UPDATE and DELETE silently affect zero rows. If the table is meant to be read-only for these roles (writes done by a table-owning or BYPASSRLS role), allowlist it as 'public.profiles_public' in [lint.rules.SEC022]. Otherwise add a policy covering the write commands — a FOR ALL policy, or a FOR INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE policy.

violations.title: Anonymous read leak (USING is unconditionally true for an unauthenticated session)
violations.message: Policy 'anyone can read profiles' on public.profiles_public leaks every row to an anonymous session. Under an unauthenticated connection every auth function (auth.uid(), auth.role(), current_setting(), …) returns NULL, and Z3 proves the USING predicate is then unconditionally TRUE for every row (three-valued / Kleene logic) — so the policy reads all rows. Every row is visible unconditionally (the predicate is constant-true under anon — it pins no row column). Gate the policy on a non-null auth check (e.g. `auth.uid() IS NOT NULL AND <tenant/owner check>`) or remove the inverting disjunct that admits anonymous. This is the semantic form of the SEC004 inverted-auth hole — see SEC004 for the syntactic variant.
